summary: Golden-query recall regressed for 5 unrelated works after ~35% one-shot corpus growth (west-eso addition, v50→v58)
description:
After guru corpus_version 50 -> 58 (four new western_esoteric texts —
kybalion, book-of-ceremonial-magic, tarot-of-the-bohemians,
psychic-self-defence — ~1,600 new chunks, roughly +35% corpus size in one
PR), 5 pre-existing golden-query recall probes on unrelated works started
failing the mustIncludeTraditions assertion in the integration gate
(src/__tests__/golden-queries.test.ts):

  - corpus-hermeticum: "why did the first heavenly man descend..." -> misses hermeticism
  - dhammapada: "a craftsman straightening a shaft..." -> misses buddhism
  - enoch-charles-1917: "who is the figure with a human face..." -> misses jewish_mysticism
  - pythagorean-golden-verses: "the Pythagorean rule of reviewing..." -> misses greek_mystery
  - tao-te-ching-legge: "the Tao Te Ching's advice to deal with..." -> misses taoism

Root-caused, ruled one hypothesis OUT:

1. RULED OUT: a new concept ("group_mind", added this same corpus update)
   whose auto-derived label "Group Mind" whole-word-matched the common word
   "mind" in extractConcepts() (src/lib/graph.ts), spuriously firing the
   graph leg into western_esoteric on unrelated queries. This was real and
   has been fixed (concept renamed to collective_psychic_field in guru's
   concepts/taxonomy.toml, todo captured in that repo) -- but re-running the
   full integration gate after the fix reproduced all 5 failures identically.
   The renamed concept's graph-leg contribution (1 chunk) never survived
   into the final top-15 in either run, confirming it was not the driver
   for these 5.

2. CONFIRMED DRIVER: plain vector-rank dilution. Checked directly for the
   dhammapada probe: its target chunk (buddhism.dhammapada-chapter-03.001)
   ranks only 102nd of 6,068 chunks by raw cosine distance for that query --
   it was always a marginal semantic match riding on favorable multi-leg
   merge/rerank behavior, not strong vector similarity. All 5 failing probes
   share this profile (none anchor strongly on vector distance alone).
   Adding ~1,600 dense new chunks in one shot was enough to tip several such
   marginal probes below the top-15 threshold after retrieve()'s
   merge-and-rerank step, even though vectorSearch's own candidate pool
   (topK * poolMult = 150) is wide enough to still include rank ~102.

This is retrieval-tuning territory (src/lib/retriever.ts's mergeAndRerank /
diversity logic, or the poolMult/lexical-leg balance), not a content or
taxonomy bug, and not something guru's own workbook fix (the concept
rename) could touch. docs/golden-queries.md's assumption that "unrelated
works... stale corpus_version only warns, never fails" appears to hold for
small incremental corpus growth but breaks down for a large one-shot
addition like this one.

Next steps for whoever picks this up: (a) decide whether these 5 probes'
wording should be re-audited/strengthened now that the corpus is larger
(the golden-queries.md draft-iterate path), or (b) investigate whether
mergeAndRerank's diversity logic should weight vector-rank more heavily
relative to lexical/graph legs as corpus size grows. Not blocking the PR
that surfaced it -- captured for separate follow-up.
